summary: MySQL is creating many on-disk internal temporary tables for a grouped workload; the evidence points to query/schema shape, especially wide grouped columns and TEXT-like rows, rather than a simple server-memory setting.
symptoms: mysqltuner reports a large fraction of temp tables created on disk
Raising tmp_table_size and max_heap_table_size from 16M to 200M reduced but did not eliminate the disk-temp-table share
The same database on another machine shows a much lower on-disk temp-table percentage
The user is considering changing table engines to address GROUP BY behavior
mechanism: MySQL internal temporary tables can spill to disk when GROUP BY / ORDER BY / UNION work has wide rows, TEXT/BLOB columns, or other row-shape limits that prevent MEMORY-based temp tables from being used efficiently. A workload with a wide grouped key, text payloads, and join fanout can keep creating disk-backed temporary tables even after tmp_table_size and max_heap_table_size are increased. Switching base tables from MyISAM to MEMORY does not change how MySQL builds internal temp tables for the query.

facts.evidence: The post says 'Of 17158 temp tables, 30% were created on disk' and earlier 'Of 23725 temp tables 38% were created on disk'.
The author says they changed max_heap_table_size and tmp_table_size from 16m to 200m and the disk-temp-table percentage dropped.
The post lists the server configuration values.
The post says another system with default configuration shows 'of 23725 temp tables, 1% were created on disk' with the same database.

disk_trigger_candidates: columns over 512 bytes used with GROUP BY / UNION / ORDER BY

facts.evidence: This is the known MySQL internal temporary-table behavior referenced by the accepted answer and consistent with the user's GROUP BY concern.

assumptions: The problematic workload includes aggregation or ordering over a wide grouped key or text-heavy rows
The high on-disk temporary-table fraction reflects query mix and row shape, not just RAM shortage
The reported mysqltuner counters are for MySQL internal temporary tables, not user-created TEMPORARY TABLE statements
unknowns: Exact SQL statements that produce the temp tables
Exact table definitions and indexes in the production database
Exact MySQL version and internal temp-table implementation details
Whether the user is observing latency, I/O pressure, or only mysqltuner counters
Whether any queries involve TEXT/BLOB, GROUP_CONCAT, or very wide VARCHAR columns
